project: URLGuard — Machine Learning Based Phishing URL Detection System
college: Jaypee Institute of Information Technology, Noida
selection_reason: Random Forest had the highest validation F1-score for the phishing class (0.9924).

features.name: url_length
features.label: URL length
features.description: Total number of characters in the normalized URL.
features.why: Some phishing links are very long because they hide the real destination or add extra tracking text.

features.name: dot_count
features.label: Number of dots
features.description: How many '.' characters appear in the full URL string.
features.why: Extra dots can come from extra host labels or from a long, messy link.

features.name: hyphen_count
features.label: Number of hyphens
features.description: How many '-' characters appear in the full URL string.
features.why: Hyphens are sometimes used to imitate a real brand name inside a hostname or path.

features.name: digit_count
features.label: Number of digits
features.description: How many numeric characters appear in the URL.
features.why: Automatically generated phishing links often contain many digits.

features.name: at_count
features.label: Number of @ symbols
features.description: How many '@' characters appear in the URL.
features.why: An @ symbol can make the real hostname harder to notice, because the browser uses the host after the @.

features.name: subdomain_count
features.label: Number of subdomains
features.description: Extra hostname labels beyond the last two labels, after a leading www is removed. example.com and www.example.com both count as 0. login.example.com counts as 1. This is a simple approximation and does not understand suffixes such as co.uk. IP addresses count as 0. www is removed because every legitimate row in this dataset starts with www.
features.why: Extra subdomains are sometimes used to imitate a trusted brand.

features.name: uses_https
features.label: HTTPS usage
features.description: 1 if the scheme is https, otherwise 0. A missing scheme is treated as https before this check.
features.why: The scheme is one signal. HTTPS encrypts traffic, but phishing websites can use HTTPS too, so it is not proof of safety.

features.name: is_ip_address
features.label: IP address usage
features.description: 1 if the hostname is an IPv4 or IPv6 address according to Python's ipaddress module, otherwise 0.
features.why: Most public websites use a domain name. A raw IP address can be suspicious, though it is not always malicious.

features.name: suspicious_keyword_count
features.label: Suspicious keywords
features.description: Total substring count of these words, matched without regard to case: login, verify, update, secure, account, confirm, password. A word inside a longer word can also match. These are weak indicators, not proof.
features.why: Words such as login, verify, and password appear in many phishing lures. They also appear on real login pages.

features.name: question_mark_count
features.label: Number of question marks
features.description: How many '?' characters appear in the URL.
features.why: A question mark usually starts a query string, which can carry extra parameters.

features.name: equals_count
features.label: Number of equals signs
features.description: How many '=' characters appear in the URL.
features.why: Equals signs usually join a query parameter to its value.

features.name: path_length
features.label: URL path length
features.description: Number of characters in the URL path returned by urllib.parse, including the leading slash when one is present.
features.why: A very long path can be used to bury the real destination of a link.

Logistic Regression.scaler: StandardScaler inside a Pipeline, fit on training data only

K-Nearest Neighbors.scaler: StandardScaler inside a Pipeline, fit on training data only

Random Forest.scaler: None. Trees do not need scaled features.

dataset.name: PhiUSIIL Phishing URL (Website)
dataset.citation: Prasad, A. & Chandra, S. (2024). PhiUSIIL Phishing URL (Website) [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cose.2023.103545.
dataset.paper: Prasad, A., & Chandra, S. (2023). PhiUSIIL: A diverse security profile empowered phishing URL detection framework based on similarity index and incremental learning. Computers & Security, 103545. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cose.2023.103545
dataset.confirmation_method: The official UCI dataset page states 'Label 1 corresponds to a legitimate URL, label 0 to a phishing URL'. The downloaded file matches the published size: 134850 rows with label 1 and 100945 rows with label 0.
dataset.official_label_sentence: Label 1 corresponds to a legitimate URL, label 0 to a phishing URL

prediction_example.note: The original phishing URL is not printed. Features were calculated on the full URL before redaction.

warnings: Scores describe a stratified subset of about 30,000 real records, not the full 235,795-row dataset.
A random split of URLs can still place related domains in both training and testing.
The phishing probability is a model score, not a calibrated guarantee of real-world risk.
